sections.content: How many people are "education advisers and school inspectors"?

26,625 people

were counted on the census as "education advisers and school inspectors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Education advisers and school inspectors organise and direct the educational activities and resources in a local authority education area, and undertake inspections of schools and other training establishments excluding universities.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "education advisers and school inspectors" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "education advisers and school inspectors", 13.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "education advisers and school inspectors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "education advisers and school inspectors" included:

  • property, housing and estate managers
  • counsellors
  • garage managers and proprietors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "education advisers and school inspectors" there were more women than men (65.3% compared with 34.7%).

This means "education advisers and school inspectors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 34.7% and women made up 65.3% of "education advisers and school inspectors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "education advisers and school inspectors" included:

  • customer service occupations (other)
  • kitchen and catering assistants
  • archivists, conservators and curators

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "education advisers and school inspectors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged between 30 and 49 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "education advisers and school inspectors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "education advisers and school inspectors", 11.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (61.8% compared with 38.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (73.3%) than self-employed (26.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
